Welcome back to Dev Opportunity Radar.

This is a weekly series where I share opportunities, resources, communities, and interesting finds that I come across, with the goal of helping people discover things they might otherwise miss.

This week's edition features Magnificent Grants, the AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship, CodePath's Fall 2026 Courses, and Interview Prep 101, a free workshop recording from CodePath's Emerging Engineers Summit packed with practical advice for technical interviews.

If you're new to the series, you can also browse previous editions, search past opportunities, and explore Community Finds, Reader Updates, and Resources Worth Checking Out on the Dev Opportunity Radar website. I've also written a short post about why I built it. You'll find links to both at the end of this article.

This week's 🌟 Community Finds section features an opportunity shared by Konark Sharma (@konark_13). Thank you, Konark, for recommending the Zero Downtime Hackathon. I always enjoy seeing readers help others discover opportunities they might otherwise have missed, and I hope this section continues to grow.

If you've discovered something through the radar, I'd love to hear about it. Whether you applied to an opportunity, attended an event, joined a community, completed a program, built something, or found a resource you hadn't seen before, I'd be happy to feature your experience in a future 💙 Reader Updates section (with your permission).

And if you've come across an opportunity, resource, community, program, event, or anything else you think deserves more attention, feel free to share it in the comments.

If I feature one of your 🌟 Community Finds in a future edition, I'll always make sure to credit you. If you discovered it, that recognition belongs to you.

📍 This Week's Opportunities

Here are a few opportunities I came across this week that I thought were worth sharing.

📌 Magnificent Grants

Who it's for: Builders, founders, researchers, creators, and ambitious young people aged 25 or younger who are working on ambitious ideas, side projects, startups, or other high-impact work. You don't need to have a company or drop out of school to apply, although showing meaningful progress on what you're building will strengthen your application.

What stands out: Magnificent Grants awards $10,000+ grants to a small group of young builders each year, along with two years of mentorship from experienced founders and investors. Unlike many startup programs, the grant comes with no equity requirement, allowing recipients to continue building independently while receiving ongoing support.

I wanted to include this because it's refreshing to see a program that's willing to support people at a very early stage. Many fellowships expect applicants to already have traction, funding, or a well-established company. Here, the focus seems to be on identifying exceptional people with ambitious ideas and helping them move faster.

Another thing I like is that the support extends well beyond the grant itself. Fellows become part of a two-year community where they receive mentorship, meet other grantees, and continue building relationships with experienced founders and investors. The fact that you don't need to drop out of school or leave your job also makes it accessible to more people who are still exploring their ideas.

Grant: $10,000+ (no equity required)

Program Duration: Two years

Who can apply: Anyone aged 25 or younger from anywhere in the world.

Application Deadline: Rolling

🔗 Learn More | 🔗 Apply

📌 AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship

Who it's for: Recent graduates, early-career researchers, and people interested in exploring how AI is shaping society. While the fellowship is primarily aimed at applicants from the social sciences and humanities, people from STEM, the arts, and other backgrounds are also encouraged to apply. Previous AI experience is welcome but not required.

What stands out: The AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship is a remote 8 to 10-week program that brings together people interested in the societal and political implications of AI. Fellows participate in weekly discussions, receive mentorship, work on a collaborative group project, attend workshops and seminars, and write their own analytical piece that will be published on the AI Societal Impact Lab website.

I wanted to include this because most AI fellowships focus on building models or developing technical skills. This one takes a different approach by exploring the broader questions around how AI is changing society and encouraging thoughtful discussions from people with different backgrounds.

Another thing I like is that you don't need to be an AI expert to apply. The fellowship welcomes people from a variety of disciplines and creates a space where different perspectives can come together. If you've been curious about AI governance, ethics, public policy, or the social impact of emerging technologies, this looks like a great place to learn and contribute.

Program Duration: Approximately 8 to 10 weeks (starting in mid to late September 2026)

Time Commitment: Around 4 hours per week

Format: Fully remote

Benefits: Mentorship, workshops and seminars, collaborative group project, publication on the AI Societal Impact Lab website, and a community of fellows.

Who can apply: Recent graduates, early-career researchers, and applicants from a wide range of backgrounds, including humanities, social sciences, STEM, and the arts.

Application Deadline: September 4, 2026 (rolling until filled)

🔗 Learn More | 🔗 Apply

📌 CodePath Fall 2026 Courses

Who it's for: Students and recent graduates in computer science or software-related programs who want to strengthen their technical skills, prepare for internships and full-time roles, and learn in a structured, instructor-led environment. Some pathways have additional prerequisites, so be sure to review the requirements before applying.

What stands out: CodePath is offering its Fall 2026 cohort of free, instructor-led technical courses in Applied AI Engineering, Technical Interview Prep, Cybersecurity, and Web Development. Each pathway runs virtually for around 10 weeks, combining live classes, hands-on assignments, projects, and mentorship from engineers at leading technology companies.

I wanted to include this because I've personally completed two CodePath courses: Intermediate Cybersecurity (with Honors) and Intro to Technical Interview Prep. They were genuinely some of the most valuable learning experiences I've had. The courses aren't passive video lectures. Every week includes live, interactive sessions, breakout discussions with peers and teaching assistants, and practical assignments that push you to apply what you've learned.

One thing I also appreciate is that CodePath expects commitment. Getting accepted isn't the final step. Every applicant is required to complete pre-work as part of the admissions process, and it takes real time and effort. It's one of the reasons the community stays so engaged. Everyone begins the course having already demonstrated they're willing to put in the work.

Another thing I like is that the experience continues well beyond the classroom. After completing a course, students gain access to career services, a large network of students and alumni, industry mentors, recruiting events, career fairs, workshops with leading technology companies, and an active Slack community where people continue learning and helping one another.

Available Pathways:

  • Applied AI Engineering
  • Technical Interview Prep
  • Cybersecurity
  • Web Development

Duration: Approximately 10 weeks

Format: Virtual, instructor-led

Cost: Free

Who can apply: Students aged 18+ who will be enrolled in a U.S. college or university during Fall 2026 in a computer science or software-related degree program. WEB101 and CYB101 are open to students from all majors. Recent computer science graduates are also eligible. Individual courses may have additional prerequisites.

Application Deadline: August 23, 2026

💡 Tip: Don't wait until the last minute. After submitting your application, you'll need to complete the required pre-work before your application can be reviewed. The pre-work takes time, so applying early gives you the best chance of completing everything before the deadline.

📚 Resources Worth Checking Out

Not every useful find comes with an application deadline.

Here's one resource worth checking out this week.

CodePath: Interview Prep 101 (Free Workshop Recording)

Who it's for: Students, new graduates, internship applicants, and anyone preparing for software engineering interviews.

What stands out: This free session from CodePath's 2024 Emerging Engineers Summit focuses on the parts of interviewing that people often overlook. Instead of diving straight into coding problems, it covers how to make a strong first impression, communicate your thought process, structure your answers, and approach technical interviews with more confidence.

I wanted to include this because interview preparation isn't just about solving LeetCode problems. Being able to clearly explain your thinking, communicate with your interviewer, and approach questions in a structured way can make a huge difference. I found this session practical and easy to follow, especially for people preparing for internships or new graduate roles.

Another thing I like is that it's only around an hour long, making it an easy resource to watch before interview season. If you're already practicing coding problems, this is a nice complement that focuses on the communication side of technical interviews.

Format: Free recorded workshop

Level: Beginner to Intermediate

Topics Covered: Technical interview preparation, communication, structuring answers, interview tips, and best practices.

🔗 Watch the Session

🌟 Community Finds

One of my favorite things about this series has been seeing people share opportunities, communities, and resources that others might not have discovered otherwise.

Zero Downtime Hackathon

Shared by Konark Sharma (@konark_13).

Konark shared the Zero Downtime Hackathon, and I thought it would be worth passing along for anyone interested in building AI applications.

The hackathon focuses on building resilient AI systems rather than just prototypes. Participants will use Port for project organization, Bright Data Scraper Studio for web data extraction, and SigNoz for observability to create an end-to-end application, pipeline, or AI agent. Projects will also be judged by engineers from Anthropic.

I wanted to feature this because it encourages participants to think beyond simply getting an AI application to work. It emphasizes planning, monitoring, and building systems that can continue running even when things change, which are skills that become increasingly important as AI projects move into production.

There are also some exciting prizes, including an NVIDIA DGX Spark AI Supercomputer for the overall winner, along with track prizes for the best integrations with each sponsor tool.

Who it's for: Developers, students, builders, and AI enthusiasts interested in building production-ready AI applications.

Format: In-person hackathon (San Francisco, California)

Event Date: August 22, 2026

Team Size: 1 to 4 participants

💙 Reader Updates

I'm looking forward to this section gradually growing over time, and I'd still love to hear from you.

One of my favorite parts of writing Dev Opportunity Radar has been hearing from people who discovered something they otherwise might have missed.

If you discovered an opportunity through the radar, applied to something, joined a community, attended an event, or simply found a resource you hadn't seen before, I'd genuinely love to hear about it.

You don't need to have been accepted or have a big success story to share. Sometimes simply discovering the right opportunity at the right time is already a win.

If you'd like to share an update, feel free to leave a comment on this edition. With your permission, I may feature it in a future 💙 Reader Updates section and tag you so other readers can celebrate your journey too.

I hope this section gradually becomes a place where we can celebrate those stories together, one update at a time.

👋 Until Next Friday

Before I go, I just want to say thank you.

Every week, I spend time searching for opportunities, resources, and communities that I think deserve a little more attention. But one of my favorite parts of this series isn't the research. It's seeing what happens after an edition is published.

Seeing someone discover an opportunity, apply to a program, share a resource, suggest a Community Find, or come back to tell us what they learned reminds me why I started Dev Opportunity Radar in the first place.

The goal has always been simple:

Help people discover opportunities they otherwise might have missed.

Thanks to all of you, it feels like we're doing exactly that.

Whether you've been reading since the very first edition or this is your first time here, thank you for being part of the journey. Every comment, suggestion, and shared opportunity helps make this series better than I could build on my own.

If you ever come across an opportunity, resource, event, community, or anything else you think deserves more attention, I'd love for you to share it in the comments. And if Dev Opportunity Radar helped you discover something exciting, I'd love to hear that too.

Thank you for reading, for sharing, and for helping make this our radar, not just mine.

I'll be back next Friday with more opportunities, resources, and Community Finds.

Until then, take care, and I hope you discover something amazing this week 💙

blocks.html_en: What stands out: Magnificent Grants awards $10,000+ grants to a small group of young builders each year, along with two years of mentorship from experienced founders and investors. Unlike many startup programs, the grant comes with no equity requirement, allowing recipients to continue building independently while receiving ongoing support.

sentences.en: What stands out: Magnificent Grants awards $10,000+ grants to a small group of young builders each year, along with two years of mentorship from experienced founders and investors.

📍本周的机会

以下是我本周遇到的一些我认为值得分享的机会。

📌 丰厚的资助

适合对象：建设者、创始人、研究人员、创造者以及 25 岁或以下雄心勃勃的年轻人，他们正在致力于雄心勃勃的想法、副项目、初创公司或其他高影响力的工作。 您不需要拥有一家公司或辍学即可申请，尽管在您正在构建的内容上表现出有意义的进展将增强您的申请。

亮点：Magnificent Grants 每年向一小群年轻建设者提供超过 10,000 美元的资助，并提供经验丰富的创始人和投资者为期两年的指导。 与许多初创项目不同，这笔赠款没有股权要求，允许接受者在获得持续支持的同时继续独立建设。

我想将其包括在内，因为看到一个愿意在很早阶段就支持人们的计划令人耳目一新。 许多奖学金希望申请人已经拥有吸引力、资金或成熟的公司。 这里的重点似乎是识别具有雄心勃勃想法的杰出人才并帮助他们更快地行动。

我喜欢的另一件事是，支持远远超出了赠款本身。 研究员成为为期两年的社区的一部分，在那里他们接受指导，会见其他受资助者，并继续与经验丰富的创始人和投资者建立关系。 事实上，你不需要辍学或离开工作，这也让更多仍在探索自己想法的人能够接触到它。

项目持续时间：两年

谁可以申请：来自世界任何地方的 25 岁或以下的任何人。

申请截止日期：滚动

亮点：AI 社会影响实验室 2026 年秋季奖学金是一项为期 8 至 10 周的远程项目，汇集了对 AI 的社会和政治影响感兴趣的人们。 研究员参加每周讨论、接受指导、开展协作小组项目、参加研讨会和研讨会，并撰写自己的分析文章，并将其发布在人工智能社会影响实验室网站上。

我想将其包括在内，因为大多数人工智能奖学金都专注于构建模型或开发技术技能。 本次会议采取了不同的方法，探索人工智能如何改变社会的更广泛问题，并鼓励不同背景的人们进行深思熟虑的讨论。

我喜欢的另一件事是，你不需要成为人工智能专家就可以申请。 该奖学金欢迎来自不同学科的人们，并创造了一个可以汇聚不同观点的空间。 如果您对人工智能治理、道德、公共政策或新兴技术的社会影响感到好奇，那么这看起来是一个学习和贡献的好地方。
